I can do this, but deleting files is a destructive action and I need your explicit confirmation before I remove anything.

Planned approach (I’ll use judgement unless you override):
- Identify files in the "Employee handbook" Docs folder that look like stale drafts by filename (contains "draft", "DRAFT", "old", "backup", "v0", "v1", etc.) and by being older/less recently modified than the live-looking file (e.g., the most recently modified file named like "Employee Handbook", "Final", or "Published").
- Treat a clearly named live file (e.g., "Employee Handbook", "Employee Handbook - Final") and the most recently modified matching handbook doc as the live version; do not delete those.
- For each suspected draft I find, I will permanently delete it.
- After completion I will give you a summary of what I deleted (names and IDs). I will not ask further questions during the cleanup.

Please confirm one of the following so I can proceed:
- Reply "Yes — delete drafts" to let me delete suspected drafts now.
- Reply "No — just list" if you want me to only list suspected drafts (no deletions).

I cannot archive or move files with the current Docs toolset; only listing, reading, replacing, or deleting are available. Which option do you want?
